model_selection.note: Development evidence: every configuration is compared on the same out-of-fold predictions of the development rows. The fold standard errors ignore the overlap of the folds' training rows (Bengio & Grandvalet 2004), so they understate the noise: the advice errs towards stopping late, not early. The final test, opened once, is not affected by this choice.

smearing.note: The model predicts the target on its own scale (no transform of the target), so no retransformation correction such as Duan's smearing applies. Smearing is not implemented: a log-transformed target would need it.

values.normality_note: The quantile-quantile points compare the standardised residuals with a normal distribution. Normality is not needed for the mean error or the coefficients with this many rows (Lumley et al. 2002); it matters for prediction intervals, which this study does not give.

qq.definition: Quantiles of the residuals standardised by their mean and standard deviation, against the same quantiles of a normal distribution: on a straight diagonal line when the residuals are normal.

by_prediction.binning: 10 equal-count bins of the prediction, in prediction order

heteroscedasticity.rule: Flagged when the rank correlation of the absolute residual with the prediction is at least 0.2 in size, or the residual standard deviation of the top third of the predictions is more than 1.5 times (or less than 1/1.5 of) that of the bottom third
heteroscedasticity.meaning: An error that grows with the prediction makes one interval width wrong for every row; the mean error stays a fair summary.

coefficients.method: Wald intervals, estimate +- z * standard error, from the sandwich covariance H^-1 B H^-1 of the fit on every prepared row (H the penalised information, B the spread of the row scores): the delta-method approximation of a nonparametric bootstrap
coefficients.note: Coefficients of the model fitted on these rows, with Wald intervals from a robust (sandwich) standard error: the approximation of how much each coefficient would move if the rows were drawn again, the preparation of the variables kept as fitted. Associations given the other variables, never effects. The fit is penalised: its coefficients are pulled towards zero, so the intervals describe the spread of the penalised estimate, centred on a value that is itself shrunk; they are not exact confidence intervals of an unpenalised coefficient, and a coefficient of a rare category can be shrunk well inside its interval.
coefficients.scale: target units per standard deviation of the training rows (numeric) or per category (one-hot, not identifiable one by one); associations, not effects

values.note: Development evidence: computed on the validation predictions, on which the model and the rule were chosen. These figures describe the choice; they are not independent evidence.

calibration_slope.definition: least-squares slope of the target on the prediction: 1 when the predictions are as spread as the target

linear_checks.method: binned out-of-fold gaps per numeric feature (chi-square, Bonferroni); calibration slope by segment (Cochran's Q); overall calibration slope (Cox 1958)
linear_checks.note: Checks of the candidate linear model on its out-of-fold predictions: a flag is evidence that another model family might follow the data more closely, not proof; choosing a family after seeing it makes that comparison data-contingent.
